warning_texts: This profile runs one vendor: the architect, four workers, five auditors and this red team are all claude-opus-5. Isolated contexts are not independent reviewers, and no GPT gate or other cross-vendor gate checks any of this work, so a chain of PASSes here is exactly what should not be trusted.
The only barriers that really hold in this run are deterministic: the machine gates, the frozen check_plan, the control lock and the release surface gate. This red-team verdict does not replace them.

Writes to the raw sources and frozen machinery were blocked by permissions.deny in .claude/settings.json for the edit tools only, not for the shell, and permissions.allow is no barrier at all. A modified raw file would be caught by the control lock after the fact, not prevented.

The inverted partner caveat passed caveats_declared, caveats_rendered, gate_claims_auditor and gate_release_auditor. Both caveat rules check for a phrase, not its meaning, so no deterministic rule anywhere in this audit can tell a caveat from its negation.

The result of every LLM auditor (gate0_semantic, gate_clean_auditor, gate_metrics_auditor, gate_claims_auditor, gate_release_auditor) and every worker is a 'driver e2e' placeholder. Each has created_at 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z, and several carry a self-check with expected and actual both 0.473684, a fig

Because of that, the unchecked territory is larger than this stage can carry. The meaning of caveats, report prose, per-figure population, dashboard n, carry content, and the renamed columns customer_id, order_date and country had no deterministic rule over them. The worker results have no disclosures field and empty warnings, so no deviation was self-reported for me to assess. Whether any stage ran an undeclared command cannot be established from the files.

All four carries list raw_data/orders.csv, the unquarantined export with the free-text column, under do_not_reread. That suggests a stage treated the raw file as something it had read. free_text_quarantined only checks pipeline.json declarations, and per the spec an undeclared read that carries noth

Pending orders (7,491; 14.1% of direct and 20.2% of partner, flat across the three months, so not recent orders still in flight) count as not completed. Excluding them would move completion from 0.724397 to 0.842857 for direct and from 0.604746 to 0.758176 for partner. The channel gap in CLM-TEST-CH

Net revenue (3,023,296.61 EUR) counts delivered orders only and excludes the 7,491 pending orders. If those deliver later, the quarter's recognised revenue grows, so the headline is a snapshot at export time and not final revenue.

The dedup_rule assumption holds on this data. For all 917 repeated order_ids, the last row in the file is also the latest by updated_at, and 126 of the repeats changed status. First-revision-wins would give net revenue 3,010,704.83 and no deduplication 3,082,640.62, against the published 3,023,296.6

The date_input_formats assumption holds on this data. The month-first reading matches order_month on all 6,852 slashed dates, against 231 for day-first. No ISO-8601 Z timestamp falls on a different Europe/Warsaw calendar day. The period is taken on order_month in any case.

The refund_sign_policy excludes 10 in-period orders: 11 raw rows have a negative refund, one of them is outside the quarter, and none has a repeat revision. That moves CLM-ORDERS by 10 and changes the completion rates only in the sixth decimal.

shipping_total recomputes exactly to 37,792,722.50 and is correctly left unpublished, but its magnitude is implausible for per-order EUR shipping. The median shipping cell is 901.14 against a median gross of 108.31, and shipping exceeds the order's gross on 39,368 orders. Nobody should cite that fig
Both p values render as '0.0000' on the report and the dashboard, although the completion test's p is about 3e-157. A reader sees an exact zero where 'p < 0.0001' would be accurate.

The dashboard test cards put the p value in 'value' under labels like 'Test Channel Completion', and no dashboard card carries a unit or its own population. A dashboard built from this JSON could show 0.0000 as though it were the channel difference.

The country mix inside each channel is stable in this quarter: every country holds 32-35% in every month. The partner caveat is wrong in what it says, not because the data happens to hide a mix shift, and the sampling-interval caveat still has to say the right thing for the next export.
